metadata.case_name: WONG PO KIN v. HOPEWELL CONSTRUCTION CO. LTD. AND OTHERS

plaintiff.occupation_before: Casual labourer; previously worked as a steel bender
plaintiff.occupation_after: Returned to work for 2nd Defendant on lighter duties (cleaning, buffing, light drills); worked as a painter (7–25 October 2000); thereafter unemployed (except brief odd job week before assessment)

injuries.description: 6% burns to his neck, face, hands and forearms.
source: the Plaintiff sustained 6% burns to his neck, face, hands and forearms.

injuries.description: Weakness of left upper limb / left hand with reduced grip and inability fully to flex left middle and index fingers.
source: the Plaintiff's left upper limp had become weaker after the Accident. The fingers of his left hand would become painful and the knuckles swollen after prolonged use of the left hand. He could not make his left hand into a tight fist and his left hand grip had weakened because he could not fully bend his left middle and index fingers to his left palm. He could not hold or lift heavy objects.
injuries.icd_description: Injury of median nerve at wrist or hand level

injuries.description: Sprained his back on 25 October 2000 (while unloading a vehicle).
injuries.icd_description: Strain or sprain of lumbar spine

injuries.description: Twisted his left ankle in about August 2001.
source: the Plaintiff twisted his left ankle in about August 2001.

manifestations.description: finely mottled scars over both forearms and some flat hypopigmented scar over the back of his left hand
these scars would become red, blotchy and itchy in hot and humid weather
unable to sweat in these areas
left hand power grip of 36 kg while the average norm should be 43.5 kg
the muscle bulk of the left upper extremity (upper arm and forearm) was less than the right side based on circumferences
weakness of the left hand power grip was quantified as "very slight"
the fingers of his left hand would become painful and the knuckles swollen after prolonged use of the left hand
could not make his left hand into a tight fist and his left hand grip had weakened because he could not fully bend his left middle and index fingers to his left palm
could not hold or lift heavy objects
should avoid tasks requiring critical grasp with heavy loading over extended periods or to support the body weight, e.g. hanging or swinging from cables or climbing scaffolding
had some reduction in his ability to lift heavy loads but such reduction was more likely to be related to the second injury (sprained back)

treatments_received: hospitalised for 4 days at Queen Elizabeth Hospital where his burns were treated conservatively
follow-up at QEH burn clinic on 28 January, 5, 10 and 19 February 1999
regular application of an ointment (Mopiko Cream)
treatments_future: ongoing use of ointment (Mopiko Cream) anticipated for years

losses.description: Residual scarring over both forearms and hypopigmented scarring over back of left hand with itching and cosmetic effects in hot and humid weather
Weakened left upper limb and reduced left hand grip preventing full fist formation and inability to lift heavy objects
Deprivation of chance to work as a steel bender (preferred occupation) and inability to perform certain steel bender duties (e.g. heavy lifting, climbing scaffolding)
